blindSummary: This state/province is an autonomous city with no regional LGTBI or gender-identity statute — the sole sub-national finding for this unit is this framework-only gap: no incident evidence, no enforcement data, and no per-city hate-offence figure was retrievable, so the absence of counts is uninformative rather than reassuring. Its religious-demographic composition and border environment parallel a neighbouring unit, though the crossing friction is less pronounced. National criminal law and the state police still apply; this unit's reporting infrastructure for gender-motivated incidents is thinner than in the larger peer units, and — unlike the capital or some peer units — no regional rollback or opposition pattern is documented: the finding is purely legislative silence.
blindSourceSummaries: A national LGBTI federation's September 2025 report on LGTBI+ education policies across the country's sub-national units; its comparative table of regional legislation is the basis for recording this unit (with two peer units) as lacking any regional LGTBI statute.

Index of the country's regional LGTBI legislation; states expressly that two small coastal units have no autonomous LGTBI laws and rely on the national framework and central-government equality policies.
